newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN PARLIAMENT TAKES HARD LINE ON IBA FRAUD.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN PARLIAMENT TAKES HARD LINE ON IBA FRAUD.

text.p: The South African parliament's public accounts committee on Friday recommended tough measures to ensure clean management of the country's many statutory commissions and watchdogs.
The recommendations were made in response to a report by the auditor-general on the abuse of corporate credit cards and other perks by members of the Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA).

The IBA, which was former to bring equity to the broadcasting industry, suspended its chief executive officer in May and five of the seven board members resigned after a probe revealed widespread use of corporate credit cards for private purchases.
The auditor-general, appointed by parliament to monitor public spending, also alleged that members had made the IBA pay for private travel and holiday accommodation.
The parliamentary committee demanded in its report that allegations of fraud should be referred to the justice department for prosecution and said that improper expenses should be recovered.
The committee said an independent auditor hired to investigate the fraud should check all IBA accounts and that parliament should form an ad hoc committee to decide on procedures for such bodies.
The special committee should set guidelines for travel, the issue and use of corporate credit cards, the extension of private loans and the standard of office accommodation.
The committee also called on the auditor general to make the auditing of new public bodies a priority.
